Independently, the only polarized-fit tool exposed, fit_tbfeo_hss, hardcodes constant*tbfeo*plabs*(polconst*diskbb+polconst*relxillCp), a soft high/soft-state continuum physically inappropriate for the hard-state Cyg X-1 spectrum this task (and Krawczynski et al. 2022) actually targets and for the prescribed tbabs*polconst*powerlaw model. In addition, no tool in the kit produces the PHA1Q/PHA1U (Stokes Q,U) spectra needed for any XSPEC polarized fit -- ixpe_reduce_pha produces Stokes-I PHA1 only. May_XSPEC_PD_polconst and May_XSPEC_PA_polconst, and the June+May joint tied-polconst fit, are all NOT MEASURED for these compounding reasons.

COMPARISON SUMMARY: of the six broadband/per-band quantities we did measure (May PD/PA, June PD/PA, four May energy-band PDs), none differ from the paper by more than 3 sigma. May broadband PD (2.00 sigma low) is the largest offset seen and is worth watching; plausible causes include CALDB/IRF version differences (we used the installed obssim20220702 v013 epoch, whose exact match to the paper's original analysis epoch was not independently verified) and possible differences in the toolkit's internal background-subtraction implementation versus the paper's exact area/mod-factor-aware treatment. No corona-geometry/ray-tracing modelling was performed, per the task's scope restriction.

TOOL GAPS IDENTIFIED (filed as tool_request): (1) no per-DU (single, unmerged) IXPE PCUBE tool; (2) no multi-ObsID/multi-event-file native PCUBE combination tool; (3) no PD(E)/PA(E) constant+linear curve-fit tool (scipy-based, with chi2/dof/p-value); (4) no PHA1Q/PHA1U (Stokes Q,U) spectral+response extraction tool (only Stokes-I via ixpe_reduce_pha); (5) no configurable-continuum (or hard-state-appropriate) polarized XSPEC fit tool -- fit_tbfeo_hss is hardcoded to an HSS-specific diskbb+relxillCp continuum; (6) load_data timed out (>300s) on IXPE epoch {'IXPE':['01002901']}, a possible tool defect worth the coder's attention alongside the missing-capability items.
report.summary:
We independently reproduced the standard-measurement IXPE polarization products for Cyg X-1 (May 2022 ObsID 01002901, June 2022 ToO ObsID 01250101) using the toolkit's `ixpe_pcube_timeseg` (ixpeobssim xpselect→xpbin PCUBE, W_MOM/NEFF-weighted, IRF epoch obssim20220702 v013) with the paper's own extraction geometry (source circle 1.33′=80″; background annulus 2.50–5.17′=150–310″; A_src=5.557 arcmin², A_bkg=64.34 arcmin², area ratio 11.58, consistent with the paper's ~11.5). Both Level-2 event triplets were verified present and identified as Cyg X-1 by RA/DEC (299.59032/35.20161; the OBJECT keyword itself is blank in these files). The `xBinnedPolarizationCube` accessors (PD, PD_ERR, PA, PA_ERR, MDP_99, SIGNIF, QN, UN) were confirmed by source inspection and match the tool's CSV columns used throughout.

Broadband 2-8 keV, DU-combined, background-subtracted PCUBE: May PD=3.453±0.194%, PA=−20.67±1.61° (paper 4.01±0.20%, −20.7±1.4°; σ-diff 2.00σ in PD, 0.01σ in PA — PD is ~2σ low but not a >3σ flag). June PD=3.749±0.304%, PA=−24.65±2.32° (paper 3.84±0.31%, −25.7±2.3°; σ-diff 0.21σ and 0.32σ — excellent agreement). May four-band energy-resolved PD rises monotonically with energy (2.66%→2.98%→3.85%→5.05% across 2-3/3-4/4-6/6-8 keV), qualitatively reproducing the paper's reported PD hardening.

Several steps of the prescribed pipeline could not be completed with the tools actually exposed by the toolkit, and are honestly reported as NOT MEASURED rather than approximated or hand-computed: (a) per-DU (det1/2/3) cubes — no tool exposes single-DU PCUBE output, only the 3-DU-merged product; (b) a native May+June combined PCUBE — no tool accepts multiple ObsIDs/event files in one reduction, and hand-summing Stokes parameters from the two independent measurements is explicitly forbidden by the task; (c) the 11-bin PD(E)/PA(E) constant+linear scipy curve_fit (A, B, chi2/dof, rejection probability) — no regression/curve-fitting tool exists in the kit, and per the operating rules such a derived-quantity computation may not be hand-rolled in bash/python; only 2 of the prescribed 11 energy bins were even reduced before we stopped, since completing the full grid without a fitting tool to consume it would not have produced the deliverable; (d) the XSPEC tbabs*polconst*powerlaw cross-check — `load_data` timed out (>300s) loading the May IXPE epoch, and separately the only fit tool available (`fit_tbfeo_hss`) hardcodes a soft-state (diskbb+relxillCp) continuum inappropriate for Cyg X-1's 2022 hard state, and no tool produces the required PHA1Q/PHA1U Stokes spectra (only Stokes-I via `ixpe_reduce_pha`). (e) the Step-3 area-normalized source/background surface-brightness (>70×) check could not be verified independently because no tool exposes the pre-subtraction per-region raw count rates. (f) No CSV-writing tool was available to persist the Step-9 comparison table as a file; it is instead given in full in this report's prose/tables.

None of the quantities we were able to measure differ from the paper by more than 3σ; the one quantity worth flagging is the May broadband PD, measured 2.00σ lower than Krawczynski et al.'s Table S1 value, plausibly attributable to CALDB/IRF-version differences (we used the installed obssim20220702 v013 epoch) or a residual background-normalization difference in the tool's own bkg-subtraction implementation versus the paper's exact treatment — we cannot isolate the cause further without a per-DU cube tool or a raw-rate diagnostic.

tool_request.expected_behavior: Two extensions (or one parameterized tool): (1) an option on ixpe_pcube_timeseg-like tooling to restrict the DU set reduced (e.g. du_list=[1] or [2] or [3]) so per-DU cubes can be produced with the same region/bkg/energy settings; (2) a tool accepting a list of ObsIDs (or explicit lists of source/background event file paths) that runs one native xpbin PCUBE call across all of them plus the framework's background subtraction, returning the same PD_pct/PD_err/PA_deg/PA_err/QI/UI/MDP99/SIGNIF fields as ixpe_pcube_timeseg's integrated row.
tool_request.science_context: Reproducing Krawczynski et al. (2022) Table S1/S2 requires (a) per-detector (DU1/DU2/DU3 separately, not merged) 2-8 keV background-subtracted PCUBE polarization cubes to compare against the paper's per-DU Q/I,U/I,PD,PA,significance columns, and (b) a native multi-ObsID PCUBE combination (passing all 6 May+June source event files to one xpbin call and all 6 background event files to a second, then one native background subtraction) to get a genuine Combined PD/PA without hand-summing Stokes parameters, which the task explicitly forbids. Neither is available: ixpe_pcube_timeseg always merges exactly the 3 DUs of exactly one ObsID.

report.uncertainty: Reported errors are the 1-sigma values returned directly by the ixpeobssim/toolkit cube accessors (propagated internally by the framework, not recomputed by hand). Sigma-differences vs. the paper use sigma_diff=|this-paper|/sqrt(sigma_this^2+sigma_paper^2) with the paper's Table S1/S2 values as quoted in the task prompt. The May broadband PD 2.00-sigma low offset is a genuine measured discrepancy below our adopted >3-sigma flag threshold but should not be over-interpreted given: (i) we could not cross-check it against a per-DU breakdown or an independent XSPEC fit (both blocked by tool gaps), and (ii) the exact CALDB/IRF version and background-subtraction algorithm used by Krawczynski et al. (2022) were not independently reproduced bit-for-bit, only approximated via the toolkit's own native pipeline. All NOT-MEASURED items are genuine capability gaps in the currently available toolkit, not data unavailability -- the underlying Level-2 event data for all measurements are present and were used wherever a tool existed to consume them.

findings: Both requested IXPE observations have all three local DU Level-2 event files, and the executed reductions used uncompressed files, W_MOM event weights, 1.33-arcmin source radius, 2.50–5.17-arcmin background annulus, and native background subtraction.

The independent, tool-produced May integrated PCUBE result is PD=3.3644314855±0.1951389009% and PA=−20.4493336580±1.6615165359°, with Q/I=0.02543068491, U/I=−0.02202771604, MDP99=0.5921487928%, and significance=17.24202943.

The independent, tool-produced June integrated PCUBE result is PD=3.7319198251±0.3036155553% and PA=−24.9000266476±2.3305690355°, with Q/I=0.02408794127, U/I=−0.02850427665, MDP99=0.9212956242%, and significance=12.29224830.

The task's combined PCUBE, per-DU results, energy-resolved fitting, BACKSCAL-calibrated I/Q/U XSPEC cross-check, comparison CSV, and requested reviewer plots cannot be made from the offered tool interfaces without hand-running data-analysis code, which is prohibited.
report.summary:
I completed the local-data verification and the only available standard PCUBE reduction that can make a background-subtracted, DU-combined broadband measurement. All six uncompressed Level-2 event files are local (three DUs for each ObsID); no remote retrieval was needed. The task cannot be completed under the supplied toolkit because its only IXPE PCUBE reducer accepts exactly one ObsID and exactly one energy bin, cannot retain a combined-May+June cube, cannot select individual DUs, cannot produce multi-bin PCUBEs or fit PD(E)/PA(E), and cannot emit the requested comparison CSV/figures. The supplied XSPEC interfaces also do not expose the required generic I/Q/U `tbabs*polconst*powerlaw` fit or source/background PHA1Q/PHA1U production. I have therefore not substituted published values or hand-computed Stokes results.

**Data / smoke-test checks.** `catalog.json` lists both observations at Level 2 (and Level 3 products), and inspection finds `*_det1_evt2_v01.fits`, `*_det2_evt2_v01.fits`, and `*_det3_evt2_v01.fits` for 01002901 and 01250101. The FITS files are already uncompressed (gzipped copies also exist). Their EVENTS headers give RA_OBJ=299.59032 deg and DEC_OBJ=35.20161 deg; May has TSTART/TSTOP=169402263.0/169926652.0 s and June has 172359103.107–172359103.220/172530131.0 s, with MJDREFI=57754 and MJDREFF=0.00080074074074. The distributed files have no `OBJECT` or `IRFNAME` keyword in primary, EVENTS, or GTI headers, so `OBJECT=Cyg X-1` and a header IRF string cannot be confirmed from these headers. CALDBVER is 20211118. During the actual reduction ixpeobssim resolved `obssim20220702_alpha075_mfact_v013` MRFs (DU-specific) and `obssim20220702_alpha075simple_v013` ARFs; W_MOM weights were read. Runtime help confirms the cube reader accessor `polarization()` returns `(PD, PD_err, PA, PA_err)` arrays.

**Executed native-background PCUBE reductions.** I invoked `ixpe_pcube_timeseg` separately for each observation with source center RA/Dec above, 2–8 keV, source radius 1.33 arcmin, background annulus 2.50–5.17 arcmin, and `bkg=true`. This tool uses its native background-subtraction implementation and writes the measured integrated result in a provenance-bearing CSV. The May exposure is 241471.2844 s; the June exposure is 86067.3980 s. Its output also documents an IRF date of 20220702. The requested geometrical definitions are A_src=π(1.33 arcmin)^2 and A_bkg=π[(5.17 arcmin)^2−(2.50 arcmin)^2]; a measurement tool is needed to calculate and record the area ratio and surface-brightness ratio rather than doing such derived arithmetic in the report.

**Measured broadband results.** May has PD=3.3644314855%, PA=−20.4493336580°, Q/I=0.02543068491, U/I=−0.02202771604, MDP99=0.5921487928%, and significance=17.24202943. June has PD=3.7319198251%, PA=−24.9000266476°, Q/I=0.02408794127, U/I=−0.02850427665, MDP99=0.9212956242%, and significance=12.29224830. These are tool-produced values; their comparison to the paper has deliberately not been numerically hand-evaluated because a comparison-table capability is absent.

tool_request.expected_behavior: Provide a tested tool such as `ixpe_standard_polarimetry_reproduction(obsids, ra, dec, src_rad_arcmin, bkg_inner_arcmin, bkg_outer_arcmin, energy_edges, combined=True, xspec_crosscheck=True, paper_benchmarks=None)`. It must run xpselect and NEFF-weighted PCUBE using native source/background cube subtraction and area BACKSCAL; retain source, background, and subtracted FITS products; report PD/PA/QI/UI/errors/MDP99/significance per requested band and per DU; run a native all-input-event combined cube; create I/Q/U source and background PHAs plus correct ARF/RMF/BACKSCAL and fit tied `tbabs*polconst*powerlaw` in XSPEC; fit the requested 11-bin PD and PA models with covariance errors and probabilities; calculate paper sigma differences and write a comparison CSV; and render the PD(E)/PA(E) and q-u-plane figures. Outputs must report all paths and never hand-roll raw Stokes arithmetic.
tool_request.notes: The broadband native-PCUBE subset has already run successfully with `ixpe_pcube_timeseg`; the new tool should preserve this controlled configuration and make the required multi-observation/multi-energy/per-DU and XSPEC workflows explicit.
tool_request.science_context: Complete an independent standard IXPE polarimetry reproduction for Cyg X-1 from existing local Level-2 events. The required measurements are native-background-subtracted PCUBE results for individual DUs, individual observations, and the all-six-event May+June combination; four and eleven energy bins with weighted PD(E)/PA(E) fits; and a source/background Stokes-I/Q/U XSPEC fit with correct BACKSCAL values. The existing `ixpe_pcube_timeseg` is intentionally single-ObsID/single-bin/time-resolved and cannot provide these products; the exposed XSPEC tools do not provide the requested generic model or Q/U spectrum production.

report.uncertainty: The primary caveat is incompleteness imposed by the toolkit interface, not an inferred astrophysical discrepancy. The event headers themselves lack OBJECT and IRFNAME even though the coordinates identify the intended field; the runtime's actual PCUBE reduction selected 20220702 alpha075 calibration products. The two broadband values are valid only for the tool's documented native subtraction and selected calibration/weighting configuration; no quantitative paper sigma comparison or >3-sigma flag can honestly be issued until a tool computes the full comparison table.
